findings.where: Destination cards (Canggu, Uluwatu, Kuta Lombok): the uppercase region label and the place name, at both widths
findings.fault: The card text is set in a typewriter-style monospace, a third typeface the brand doesn't have. Card titles should be Quicksand 600 and labels Nunito Sans. The place names look like code or placeholder text, not the brand's rounded, friendly type, and they look nothing like the rest of the page.
findings.who_objects: A backpacker comparing destinations sees a block that looks unfinished or borrowed from another site. The founder would also object, because the brand sheet sets the typefaces and the north star names a sterile look as the enemy.

findings.where: The 'Where we're starting' section heading, against the hero's MantaHostels title and claim (worst at desktop, where it fills two lines at about twice the hero title's size)
findings.fault: The size order is upside down. The section heading for three small cards is set far bigger than the hero's main title, so it reads as the page's headline. The hero, which says what MantaHostels is, looks secondary by comparison.
findings.who_objects: A first-time visitor scanning the page takes 'Where we're starting' as the main message and the hero as a lead-in. On desktop it fills the bottom of the first screen and pushes the cards it introduces out of view.

findings.where: Desktop nav bar: 'Destinations' and 'How we rank'
findings.fault: Two links side by side in the same nav are styled differently: 'How we rank' is underlined and 'Destinations' isn't. If the underline is meant to mark the current page, it is the reverse of the house rule, which says the current link drops its underline and turns semibold.
findings.who_objects: A visitor reads the underlined link as different, perhaps as the current page or as something to click first, when the two links do the same kind of job. The founder would object because it breaks the nav's current-page rule.
